passage: Note, Friday, from Dolma (PE teacher). After the district football semi-final loss, the head coach spoke loudly to the team for a long while. Sahil, age 10, stood at the back with his eyes on his boots and his shoulders up near his ears. When asked why he missed the pass, he said nothing. Afterwards he sat on the bench and told me quietly that he felt small. I said the points about passing and positions were worth remembering, but the loud tone was not a measure of him. We wrote down two points together. I told him that if anyone ever makes him truly scared or hurt, he should tell his parents. I will also speak to the head coach about the tone.

qa.q: What does Sahil's posture and silence suggest about how he felt after the loss?
qa.a: That he felt scared and small: his eyes were on his boots, his shoulders were up, and he told Dolma quietly that he felt small.

qa.q: How could Sahil separate the useful points from the harsh tone?
qa.a: By writing down the points about passing and positions, as they did together, and letting the loud tone go.

qa.q: How might the head coach see the situation?
qa.a: Probably as wanting the team to improve after a loss, though Dolma plans to speak to them because the tone left a child scared.

grounding: A coach is angry after a loss and the child feels scared and small; a teacher notes the useful points, separates the tone and reminds him to tell parents.
